messages:
alex: Observed steady GPU memory growth on prod GPUs when we handle long-context streams. Correlation looks strong with continuous-batching merge activity + sharp drop in KV reuse. Root repro attached.
maria: repro? any quick logs or numbers to share?
alex: repro on my laptop with the longctx warmup script. pprof flamegraph points to a tight loop in merge path. Top frames: kv_cache::evict_entry, contbatch::merge_batches, kernel_selector::choose_kernel.
cheng: kernel selection on the hot path could be making merges slower and holding refs longer — that would increase fragmentation and reduce reuse.
sam: saw a similar incident last month where merge_abort spiked during long contexts, ended up being a slot alignment bug. Any "merge_abort" lines in the logs?
alex: yes, lots of them. small log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z evict: slot=1248 age=847ms
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z merge_abort: src_batch=63 dst_batch=62 reason=slot_mismatch
2026-03-12T14:02:12Z contbatch_wait: 82ms
```
maria: can you post the perf numbers? cpu/% time and memory delta over the run?
alex: perf summary from a 10m run: 
```
# perf top (sampled)
40.1% kv_cache::evict_entry
22.3% contbatch::merge_batches
10.4% kernel_selector::choose_kernel
```
Memory: resident +1.8GB over 10m on longctx traffic vs +200MB baseline. Reuse_rate counter dropped from 87% -> 42% during the spike.
cheng: interesting. two immediate hypotheses: (A) kernel_selector picks a path that forces extra per-token state causing larger per-slot footprint, (B) merge_abort churn leaves many small fragments that never coalesce so eviction works harder.
maria: easy experiment: force a single kernel for all requests in a canary cluster and compare. also add counters for frag_rate and reuse_rate to be safe.
alex: I built a branch that forces kernel_A for all codepaths and it reduced merge CPU by ~30% in the repro. Repro command: `git checkout kv/fast-merge-force-kA && ./repro/longctx_contbatch.sh` :thumbsup:
perf-bot: ALERT: contbatch head_of_line latency >200ms on cluster-3 for service=inference-rt (2026-03-13T03:41:02Z)
sam: seeing perf-bot alert too. we should run the forced-kernel canary on two hosts and run a 24h soak to measure token cost, p99 latency, and evict rate.
cheng: I can prototype a compact-on-abort routine: when merge_abort occurs, try a lightweight compaction step for that slot to reduce fragmentation. cheap and optimistic.
maria: I'll add the frag_rate/reuse_rate counters and a dashboard comparison (baseline vs forced-kernel). also plan a canary rollout script that toggles kernel selector flag.
alex: created PR #1428 with flamegraphs, perf summary, and reproducer steps. baseline vs forced-kernel traces attached in the PR.
sam: ack, I will review the PR and kick off the canary tonight. if we see the reuse_rate recover and memory delta stabilizes we'll push to staging.
alex: action items recorded: (1) metrics (maria), (2) forced-kernel canary (maria/sam), (3) compact-on-abort patch (cheng), (4) PR review and soak (sam). I'll post soak results here tomorrow morning :eyes:
maria: noted, adding alerts for frag_rate > 10% and reuse_rate < 60% to catch early signs.
cheng: also adding a microbenchmark to simulate long contexts + contbatch merges to exercise cornercases. will post results.
sam: thanks all. if anyone finds an easy patch to avoid slot_mismatch merge_aborts please ping me immediately.
